claims.text: What the strip looks like Chaotic, irregular deflections with no identifiable QRS complexes — immediately fatal without defibrillation.
claims.quote: Ventricular Fibrillation: Chaotic, irregular deﬂections without identiﬁable QRS complexes. Immediately fatal without deﬁbrillation.

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Waveform: chaotic irregular deflections of varying amplitude; no identifiable P waves, QRS complexes or T waves
claims.quote: Chaotic irregular deflections of varying amplitude No identifiable P waves, QRS complexes, or T waves

claims.text: Amplitude: falls the longer it lasts — coarse VF, then fine VF, then asystole as myocardial energy runs out
claims.quote: Prolonged ventricular fibrillation results in decreasing waveform amplitude, from initial coarse VF to fine VF, ultimately degenerating into asystole due to progressive depletion of myocardial energy stores

claims.text: Causes (mechanism and diagnoses) Mechanism: the ventricles fire at up to 500/min with no coordinated contraction — immediate loss of cardiac output
claims.quote: The ventricles suddenly attempt to contract at rates of up to 500 bpm This rapid and irregular electrical activity renders the ventricles unable to contract in a synchronised manner, resulting in immediate loss of cardiac output

claims.text: Cardiac: ischemia/infarction, cardiomyopathy (dilated, hypertrophic, restrictive), channelopathies (long QT → torsades → VF; Brugada), aortic stenosis, aortic dissection, myocarditis, tamponade, blunt trauma (commotio cordis)
claims.quote: Myocardial ischemia / infarction Cardiomyopathy (dilated, hypertrophic, restrictive) Channelopathies e.g. Long QT (acquired / congenital) causing TdP –> VF and Brugada syndrome Aortic stenosis Aortic dissection Myocarditis Cardiac tamponade Blunt trauma (Commotio Cordis)

claims.text: Respiratory: tension pneumothorax, pulmonary embolism, primary pulmonary hypertension, sleep apnea, bronchospasm, aspiration
claims.quote: Tension pneumothorax Pulmonary embolism Primary pulmonary hypertension Sleep apnoea Bronchospasm Aspiration

claims.text: Toxic, environmental, other: drugs (e.g., verapamil in AF with WPW), drug-induced long QT with torsades, electric shock, drowning, hypothermia, sepsis, seizure, stroke
claims.quote: Toxic and Metabolic Drugs (e.g. verapamil in patients with AF+WPW) Drug-induced QT prolongation with torsades de pointes Environmental Electrical shocks, drowning, hypothermia Sepsis Neurological Seizure CVA

claims.text: With ischemic heart disease, VF may be preceded by PVCs, ST changes, R on T, sinus pause, QT prolongation, VT, supraventricular arrhythmias or sinus tachycardia
claims.quote: In the presence of ischaemic heart disease VF may be preceded by: Premature ventricular contractions (PVCs) ST changes R on T phenomenon Sinus pause QT prolongation Ventricular tachycardia Supraventricular arrhythmias Sinus tachycardia

claims.text: Symptoms Immediate syncope and death within minutes
claims.quote: It causes immediate syncope and death within minutes.

claims.text: Treatment CPR with defibrillation, starting at biphasic 120–200 J (or monophasic 360 J)
claims.quote: Treatment of ventricular fibrillation is with cardiopulmonary resuscitation, including defibrillation, beginning with biphasic 120 to 200 joules (or monophasic 360 joules).

claims.text: Refractory VF (no pulse after the first 2 shocks): defibrillate every 2 minutes and give epinephrine every 3–5 minutes; amiodarone or lidocaine if still shockable after 3 shocks and epinephrine
claims.quote: For patients in refractory VF or pulseless VT who do not achieve return of pulses after the first 2 defibrillation attempts, repeat defibrillation is done every 2 minutes and epinephrine is given every 3 to 5 minutes. Amiodarone or lidocaine may also be given if the patient continues in a refractory shockable rhythm despite 3 shocks and administration of epinephrine.

claims.text: After VF with no reversible or transient cause: high risk of recurrence and sudden death — most need an ICD
claims.quote: Patients who have VF without a reversible or transient cause are at high risk of future VF events and of sudden death. Most of these patients require an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator
